events.title: Some women gain the vote
events.summary: A UK law let some women aged 30 or over vote. Many women still could not vote.
events.staff_precision: The Representation of the People Act 1918 received Royal Assent on 6 February 1918. Women aged at least 30 needed qualifying electoral/property status, or qualifying husbands. Most men aged at least 21 could vote, with younger service voters also eligible. This was not equal voting rights for all women.

events.title: Montgomery bus boycott begins
events.summary: Black people and their supporters stopped using buses in Montgomery. They aimed to end rules that kept Black and White riders apart.
events.staff_precision: This is the boycott start, not Rosa Parks's arrest on 1 December 1955. The boycott challenged racial segregation on buses. No arrest or violence scene is reproduced.

events.title: March on Washington
events.summary: People marched in Washington, DC, to call for jobs and equal rights. It was a peaceful mass protest.
events.staff_precision: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, 28 August 1963. No speeches or signs are reproduced. Participants held many roles in a movement, rather than a single person's achievement.

events.title: Civil Rights Act becomes law
events.summary: A US law banned unfair race rules in many public places and at work. People still had to act to make the law work.
events.staff_precision: Civil Rights Act signed into law on 2 July 1964. It prohibited segregation in public accommodations and employment discrimination. Avoid claiming every form of discrimination ended or law alone instantly changed daily life.

events.title: Voting Rights Act becomes law
events.summary: A US law helped protect the right to vote. It aimed to stop unfair rules that kept Black voters out.
events.staff_precision: Voting Rights Act signed into law on 6 August 1965. It strengthened federal protection against racial discrimination in voting. Legal rights still required implementation and enforcement.

source_label: Teacher-written factual summaries for learning. These are not historical quotations, testimony or archive extracts.
selection_limit: Five selected rights and protest events in the UK and the United States. This is a short selection, not the whole story of rights.
